relations.subject: backup:cluster-backup
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused (behavesDifferentlyUnder) - a hard quantitative cap specific to Azure, with a direct cost consequence, exactly the shape this batch's hypothesis anticipated for backup/restore
relations.evidence: If you use Cloud Snapshot backups on an Azure cluster, Azure limits your total number of incremental backups to a maximum of 500. After 500 snapshot backups, Azure starts using full cluster backups. If you exceed 500 snapshot backups stored on your Azure-hosted cluster, your cluster backup costs will greatly increase.

relations.subject: backup:cross-region-backup-copy
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused (behavesDifferentlyUnder) - cross-region copy is supported on AWS and Azure but not GCP, a genuine three-way provider split
relations.evidence: When you take a cluster backup on an AWS or Azure cluster running Couchbase Server version 7.6.6 and later, you can choose to copy your backup to 2 additional regions.

relations.evidence: For clusters hosted on GCP, cluster backups cannot be replicated to another region.

relations.subject: backup:cluster-backup

relations.evidence: You cannot choose to use CMEK for a cluster backup if your cluster is not already encrypted with a CMEK. Bucket backups still do not support CMEK.

notable_absence.finding: This page (a mechanics/concept reference for cluster backups) states no capella-role:* or support-plan/billing-plan gate on WHO can take or restore a cluster backup - those gates are stated on the companion procedural pages (take-cloud-snapshot.md, restore-cloud-snapshot.md) as Project Owner/Organization Owner, not here. Consistent with backup-restore.json's identical finding for bucket backups: role gating and mechanics/cost description are kept on separate pages throughout this batch.

cross_product_finding: Directly answers half of this batch's hypothesis: cluster-backup billing is explicitly CSP-usage-based, not support-plan-gated - 'Capella bases your billing for your cluster backups on the backup storage usage reports from your CSP' - and the clearest concrete cost-and-behavior variance found in the whole batch is the Azure 500-incremental-snapshot cap (after which Azure silently switches to costlier full backups), plus GCP's flat exclusion from cross-region replication. This is a genuine, non-trivial provider-substrate difference in the backup/restore surface, structurally similar to round 6's Azure storage-handling finding but specific to snapshot/replication mechanics rather than storage-engine behavior.
